dublin_core_group.description:
VNP46A4 - VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Yearly L3 Global 15 arc second Linear Lat Lon Grid

The Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (SNPP) Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) supports a Day-Night Band (DNB) sensor that provides global daily measurements of nocturnal visible and near-infrared (NIR) light that are suitable for Earth system science and applications. The VIIRS DNB's ultra-sensitivity in lowlight conditions enable us to generate a new set of science-quality nighttime products that manifest substantial improvements in sensor resolution and calibration when compared to the previous era of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program/Operational Linescan System's (DMSP/OLS) nighttime lights image products. Such improvements allow the VIIRS DNB products to better monitor both the magnitude and signature of nighttime phenomena, and anthropogenic sources of light emissions.

VNP46A4 is the short-name for the fourth nighttime lights (NTL) product in the Black Marble suite, which provides yearly composites generated from daily atmospherically- and lunar-BRDF-corrected NTL radiance to remove the influence of extraneous artifacts and biases. Known by its long-name, VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Yearly L3 Global 15 arc-second Linear Lat Lon Grid, this product contains 28 layers. They provide information on the NTL composite, the number of observations, quality, and standard deviation for multi-view zenith angle categories (near-nadir, off-nadir, and all angles), their snow-covered and snow-free statuses besides land-water mask, latitude and longitude coordinate information. They also include detailed information and description of the quality flags. This SNPP VIIRS collection-1 product record, identified by its version-ID 001 in its file name, starts from January 1st 2012.

iso_group.process_step:
#########
# GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
# and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
####

#########
# Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
####

# create directory structure and move into it
mkdir -p /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/download -p /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/etl
chmod -R 777 /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4
cd /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4

# set update flag based on last update and update frequency
do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1

# load egom_2019_viirs_vnp46a4 as dependency (see egom_2019_viirs_vnp46a4 for details).

# clip raster with geometry as:
  gdalwarp -cutline PG:"<postgres connection>" -csql "SELECT geom FROM fl_2022_tl_cousub WHERE countyfp='086'" -crop_to_cutline -s_srs EPSG:4326 -t_srs EPSG:4326 -srcnodata 65535 -dstnodata 65535 /data/egom_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/download/VNP46A4.A2019001.h09v06.002.2025134123459.h5.tif download/VNP46A4.A2019001.h09v06.002.2025134123459.tif
 
#########
# Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
####

# load raster into postGIS with:
    raster2pgsql -s 4326 -d -C -I -t auto VNP46A4.A2019001.h09v06.002.2025134123459.tif -F mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4 > load_raster.sql
psql <connection options> < load_raster.sql
rm load_raster.sql

# create color raster
mkdir -p /tiles/raster/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4
mkdir -p /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived
cd /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4
cat > /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4_color_ramp.txt <<_EOF
nv 0 0 0 0
1500 252 255 164 255
1333 247 208 60 255
1166 251 154 7 255
1000 237 105 37 255
833 206 68 70 255
666 165 45 96 255
500 120 28 109 255
333 76 12 107 255
166 27 12 65 255
0 0 0 4 255
_EOF
gdaldem color-relief download/VNP46A4.A2019001.h09v06.002.2025134123459.tif /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4_color_ramp.txt /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4_color.tif -alpha
# create color raster and render raster tiles 
mkdir -p /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived
mkdir -p /tiles/raster/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4
cd /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4
echo "" | base64 -d > /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4_legend.png
cp /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4_legend.png /tiles/raster/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/
# render raster tiles 
cd /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/
gdal2tiles.py -ex --xyz -z 8-12 /data/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4/derived/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4_color.tif /tiles/raster/mdc_2019_viirs_vnp46a4
